title: Environment Diagrams
subtitle: SICP's environment model in Python: frames, parents, and local state
description: Trace the frames a call creates, find the binding a name refers to, see why a function resolves free names where it was defined, and explain how make_withdraw keeps private state. Then build definition, assignment and call frames in a small frame model.
estimateNote: Author estimate, not learner-measured: lesson 20-25 minutes (about 2,400 words of prose, eight code blocks, three figures); lab 40-55 minutes (five exercises written from stubs, about 6-15 minutes each). Reference reading excluded.
sourceAttribution: Follows section 3.2 (The Environment Model of Evaluation) of Structure and Interpretation of Computer Programs by Harold Abelson and Gerald Jay Sussman with Julie Sussman, using the book's examples (sum-of-squares, make-withdraw, sqrt with internal definitions) translated to Python; prose, figures and exercises are original.
